questions.stem:
Statements: V < X > P = W > R.
Conclusions: I. W ≤ V   II. R > P.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
Statements: S = W > T < U = Q.
Conclusions: I. U ≥ S   II. S ≤ W.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
Statements: W = R < T > U > V.
Conclusions: I. R ≥ V   II. R ≤ U.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Either I or II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. Together the alternatives cover every permissible ordering, so either I or II follows.

questions.stem:
Statements: S > X > U < Q < R.
Conclusions: I. Q > S   II. X < S.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some deposits are cheques. All cheques are lockers. No lockers is a bonds.
Conclusions:
I. Some deposits are lockers.
II. Some cheques are bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few deposits are cheques. Some cheques are lockers. All lockers are bonds.
Conclusions:
I. All deposits are bonds.
II. No cheques is a bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few deposits are cheques. All cheques are lockers. No lockers is a bonds.
Conclusions:
I. Some deposits are not cheques.
II. No cheques is a bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: No deposits is a cheques. Some cheques are lockers. All lockers are bonds.
Conclusions:
I. All deposits are bonds.
II. Some bonds are cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 54 km south, turns left and walks 90 km, then turns left and walks 6 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 102. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 48 km along the initial direction and 90 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(48² + 90²) = 102 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 34 km east, turns right and walks 72 km, then turns right and walks 4 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 78. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 30 km along the initial direction and 72 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(30² + 72²) = 78 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 18 km north, turns left and walks 16 km, then turns left and walks 6 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 20. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 12 km along the initial direction and 16 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(12² + 16²) = 20 km.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
banking growth secure = pa ka to
banking access savings = mi ka re
growth access digital = re to vo
secure savings digital = mi vo pa
banking growth digital = vo to ka
What is the code for “banking”?
questions.explanation: Answer: ka. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: banking = ka, growth = to, secure = pa, access = re, savings = mi, digital = vo.

questions.stem: B is the only daughter of F. F is the father of B. G is the son of B. A is the sister of F. How is F related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. F is the father of B, and B is G’s mother. Thus F is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: A is the mother of E. G is the daughter of E. B is the father of E. How is G related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. B is a parent of E, and G is E’s daughter. Hence G is B’s grandchild.

questions.stem: B is the brother of D. D is the mother of A. F is the father of B and D. How is B related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. B is the brother of A’s mother D. Therefore B is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: [Bar set] What is the difference between the total at B and the total at E?
questions.explanation: Answer: 900. Derived data: A: first category 560, second category 420; B: first category 1500, second category 900; C: first category 480, second category 360; D: first category 1360, second category 1020; E: first category 900, second category 600. Absolute difference = |2400 − 1500|.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 46 and 69 hours. An outlet empties it in 138 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank. (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 34.5. Net rate = 1/46 + 1/69 − 1/138 = 2/69 tank/hour. Required time = 34.5 hours.

questions.stem: The average weight of 23 people is 57 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 81. New total minus old total = (23+1)×(57+1) − 23×57 = 81.

questions.stem: A container holds 80 litres of pure milk. 16 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 51.2. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 80 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹2300 each. One earns 25% profit and the other incurs 10% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 4395.56. Recover each cost separately: 2300×100/125 + 2300×100/90. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹20000 earns ₹3000 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding?
questions.explanation: Answer: 22050. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 5%. Compound amount = 20000 × (1 + 5/100)².

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 20%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹1800. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 16.67. New quantity / old quantity = 100/120. Reduction percentage = 20/120 ×100.

questions.stem: A boat covers 48 km in still water in 4 hours. If the stream flows at 2 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 2 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 20. Still-water speed = 12 km/h. Upstream speed = 12 − 2. Distance = speed × 2.

questions.stem: A 140 m train moving at 90 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 10.8 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 6.36. Relative speed = (90 − 10.8) ×5/18 = 22 m/s. Time = 140/22.
